result.summary: Fixes getblocks/getheaders handling so that a locator advertising an oversized hash count is rejected and the peer disconnected before hash allocation, rather than failing generic deserialization and leaving the peer connected. Adds a dedicated LimitedVectorExceededError to serialize.h so LIMITED_VECTOR callers can distinguish size-limit failures from other deserialization errors, and extracts a shared ReadBlockLocator helper used by both message handlers. Includes a characterization test and a new net_tests case, plus a functional test verifying the boundary at 101/102 hashes.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core enforces MAX_LOCATOR_SZ only after deserializing the locator's hashes; a peer that advertises an oversized count but sends a truncated payload triggers a generic stream failure before the size check runs, so the misbehaving peer is never disconnected. This weakens the node's enforcement of locator-size limits against malformed or adversarial peers.

resolved_concerns: jeanpablojp found that counts above ReadCompactSize's MAX_SIZE still bypassed disconnection; author fixed it by reading the count with range_check=false and widening to uint64_t, confirmed by the reporter's re-test description.

mzumsande and sedited asked why not reuse the HEADERS-style local read instead of adding CBlockLocator::LimitedRead and a new exception type; ajtowns explained the HEADERS approach is a special case due to a serialize/deserialize format mismatch and argued the new approach preserves encapsulation better, with no further objection.
ajtowns's naming nit about s.ignore(4) vs s.ignore(sizeof(DUMMY_VERSION)) was addressed by author with a rationale (documents intent) and not pushed further.

result.card: This PR closes a gap in getblocks/getheaders handling where a peer sending a truncated locator with an oversized advertised hash count was not disconnected, because generic vector deserialization failed before the existing MAX_LOCATOR_SZ check ran. It adds a dedicated LimitedVectorExceededError to the shared LimitedVectorFormatter so callers can distinguish size-limit failures, and a shared ReadBlockLocator helper for both message types. Reviewer jeanpablojp found and confirmed a deeper variant of the bug (counts above ReadCompactSize's MAX_SIZE also bypassed disconnection), which the author fixed with a force push, and a design question about matching the existing HEADERS-style local-parsing approach was resolved by ajtowns's explanation without further objection. The PR is ready for fresh review since existing ACKs from achow101 and jeanpablojp predate the latest fix. No stated dependencies or blockers; conflicts noted with two unrelated open PRs (#36244, #35027) touching overlapping files.
